judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Securities Administrator and the Master Servicer and each of its officers' uses a singular possessive for two indemnitees, an antecedent slip corrected only in the following sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the Securities Administrator's indemnity in the preceding paragraph and uses the same 'Depositor Information' construct as the Article I definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each of its respective officers' is grammatically incoherent, and the second sentence indemnifies only the Depositor while the first indemnifies both the Depositor and the Securities Administrator.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That asymmetry does not match the parallel Securities Administrator and Depositor indemnities, both of which run to two indemnitees in each sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties' supplies no method at all, and 'the defaulting party' is used without definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a fallback to the three indemnities in Section 4.18(b) and does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single survival sentence with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the indemnities it preserves and with Section 4.17's post-termination reporting duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall, constitute an Event of Default' contains a stray comma, and the final sentence's carve-out for failures caused by another party's non-delivery sits directly against the automatic deeming language earlier in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to termination 'pursuant to this Section 4.18(d)' although this text is in Section 4.18(b) and Section 4.18(d) is the notice-delivery provision, and it is the third paragraph in Article IV to declare that it 'shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement', overriding the Section 9.01 Event of Default definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence whose meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides Section 12.01, the amendment provision, joining the Eligible Account definition and Section 4.19(d) in carving amendment rights out of that section without Certificateholder consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive delivery mechanic with named contact details; nothing open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits telephonic notification where Section 12.05 sets out the Agreement's formal notice regime, a minor divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will be supplemented and modified as necessary to be consistent with any such amendments, interpretive advice or guidance, convention or consensus among active participants in the asset-backed securities markets, advice of counsel, or otherwise' is about as open-ended as a contractual obligation can be, and 'any such amendments' has no antecedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (d) states that 'no amendment of this Agreement shall be required' to change the parties' obligations, which cannot be reconciled with Section 12.01's amendment machinery or with the Certificateholder protections it contains.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence that imposes a filing duty only where 'required by any change in the Uniform Commercial Code', saying nothing about initial filings, and 'the Seller' is used in the singular for a two-entity defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01 effects the conveyance as a sale rather than a secured loan, and there is no other perfection provision, so this stub does not sit comfortably with the transaction structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party' attributes the option to the Seller when the option is given to Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder, and the reinstatement rule ties exercise to 'the first day of the related Fiscal Quarter' although no quarterly cycle is used anywhere else in the option.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Purchase Price definition does cover Section 4.21 purchases, but the Principal Funds definition also treats Section 4.21 repurchases as made by 'the related Originator, Saxon (or its assignee) or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder', a wider group than this section confers the right on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Investment direction is given to the Majority Class CE Certificateholder, but the very next sentence makes the default turn on 'the absence of written instructions to the Securities Administrator', so it is unclear whose instructions govern.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Supplemental Interest Trust is established 'Pursuant to the Swap Administration Agreement', whereas the Supplemental Interest Trust definition says it is 'created pursuant to Section 4.22 of this Agreement'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and specific about deposits, titling and tax characterisation; the deemed-direction language ('has been directed by the Class CE Certificateholders') is a legal fiction but a clearly stated one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Reserve Fund and Reserve Fund Deposit definitions both say the fund is created pursuant to Section 6.08, whereas this is the provision that actually establishes it; the account is also titled in the Trustee's name though established by the Securities Administrator.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence ('subordinated to distributions to the Holders of the Class A, Class M and Class'), so the subordination it creates is incomplete on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs that swap payments 'shall be deducted from Interest Funds, and ... from Principal Funds', yet the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions already subtract the same Net Swap Payments and Swap Termination Payments, raising a double-deduction problem.
